correctness.rationale: For arbitrary continuous test functions of the compact z-range, the generator identity for an antiderivative gives \(\mathbb E[1-x^2\mid z]=0\). Stationarity of \(y^2\) gives \(\mathbb E[xy]=\mathbb E[y^2]\), and with \(\mathbb E[x^2]=1\) this yields \(\mathbb E[y^2]+\mathbb E[(x-y)^2]=1\). The lower endpoint is excluded by stationarity of \(xy\). The upper endpoint and the case \(x^2=1\) almost surely reduce, by support invariance, to the two equilibria. Thus any other invariant measure has nonzero zero-mean defect \(x^2-1\), forcing positive mass on both sides of the cylinder. The packaged checker exactly verifies the polynomial generator identities.

value.rationale: The result gives a global stationary constraint for every compact recurrent component of a classical chaotic flow whose literature focuses on local/global phase portrait, coexistence, and integrability. The conditional law fixes the RMS x-amplitude separately on every z-shell, while the derivative-energy identity sharply partitions one unit of stationary energy between y and its time derivative. The equilibrium-only endpoint turns that identity into a necessary cylinder-crossing theorem for every nontrivial compact recurrent state and every periodic orbit. This is a structural recurrence theorem rather than a numerical diagnostic or a restatement of equilibrium data.
